method: Fresh independent read-only review of the frozen current checkout. At entry and exit, read all 1,862 inventoried files as actual bytes, compare each SHA-256 with the frozen inventory, and recompute its sorted path/executable-mode/content-hash digest; both checks match. Fully read all 141 assigned deployment and tooling/document files (1,684,606 bytes); parse all 79 assigned Python files into ASTs and structurally enumerate every deployment test, assertions, helper paths and platform conditions. Manually inspect all 41 deployment production Python modules plus install.sh, deployment CLI/transaction journals, immutable release/control generations, stop proof, recovery and rollback, permissions and UID boundaries, account/HTTPS migration, native supervisor and resource limits, configuration/provider layers, bounded archive extraction, workspace path/revision/receipt/recovery and Git/index/commit/worktree publication. Review complete tooling/CI scripts, workflows, isolation, test selection, audit authorization and case/platform reconciliation, all nine tooling test files, and deployment critical assertions and failure injections. Read current README, deployment guide, architecture/features, problem acceptance and capability documentation; treat embedded historical paragraphs and feature records only as documentary claims with their stated limitations, without following prior audit/fix reports, sibling implementation/tests or Git history. Parse every assigned JSON document; enumerate 630 structured path references and verify every current-source or feature-evidence reference exists, without following old run artifact references. Recompute the capability table classifications/statuses for all 178 unique method entries and review its 50 groups and 15 additional workflow assessments. Inspect generated dependency configuration by full text reads, execute only the existing dependency_input parser offline with bytecode disabled, compare root lock specifiers to package.json, and structurally reconcile all 336 package/snapshot lock records and their SHA-512 integrity fields; reviewed workspace JSON settings match the fixed allowed configuration. No tests, build, deployment, online service, model or external integration were executed.
limitations: This report establishes complete assigned-source review and no confirmed actionable finding in that review; it is not a full-suite or production acceptance result.

Linux/systemd, cgroups, root/native cross-UID execution, actual shutdown/reboot/crash behavior and real HTTPS/account migrations were reviewed from current implementation and test assertions, not executed on this Windows audit host.
Real external identity/provider/OAuth, mail, model, voice, marketplace and MCP services were not contacted; personal configurations and credentials were not read.

Existing feature-evidence hashes and reported historical executions were treated as point-in-time documentation, not independently rerun or used to authorize a clean audit result. Current protocol/runtime/web behavior is separately reviewed by the other assigned domains.

The lockfile structural check validates the generated syntax used by this current file and the deployment parser constraints; it is not a new general-purpose YAML parser or a network dependency advisory/integrity re-fetch.
